# Context

Colour is a trait: stay-green, senescence, seed colour, disease. A **vegetation index** combines the colour channels in one number that highlights what we want. We also measure the **percentage of diseased leaf area** without rating each leaf by eye.

```{r packages}
library(pliman)
library(dplyr)
```

# Colour of seeds

```{r soy}
soy <- image_pliman("soy_green.jpg", plot = FALSE)
plot(soy)
```

```{r indices, fig.height = 3}
image_index(soy, index = c("R", "GLI", "NGRDI"), ncol = 3, nrow = 1)
# GLI is high for green tissue; NGRDI separates green from yellow and red
```

```{r seed-colour, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 3.2}
colour <- analyze_objects(soy, marker = "id", object_index = c("NGRDI", "GLI"), verbose = FALSE)
colour$object_index |> mutate(across(-id, \(x) round(x, 3)))
# Seeds 5 and 9 are greener: higher GLI, NGRDI close to zero (-0.03 against about -0.08)
```

```{r threshold}
# HINT: seeds with NGRDI above -0.05 are green. Which threshold gives two groups?
colour$object_index |>
  mutate(class = if_else(NGRDI > ___, "green", "yellow")) |>      # TODO
  count(class)
# You should get 2 green and 7 yellow seeds
```

**Your findings:** a threshold found on 9 seeds: is it enough to classify a whole trial? How would you set it so that it can be trusted? _...write here..._

# Flax leaves: elongated objects

```{r flax-leaves}
fleaves <- image_pliman("flax_leaves.jpg", plot = FALSE)
plot(fleaves)
```

```{r watershed, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
split_default <- analyze_objects(fleaves, marker = "id", verbose = FALSE)
# HINT: long leaves are cut in pieces by the watershed. Switch it off
whole <- analyze_objects(fleaves, marker = "id", watershed = ___,        # TODO
                         object_index = c("NGRDI", "GLI"), verbose = FALSE)
c(default = nrow(split_default$results), whole = nrow(whole$results))     # you should get 28 and 15
```

**Your findings:** the default gives 28 objects and there are 15 leaves. Why? _...write here..._

# A senescence score, and your own eye

```{r senescence}
leaf_traits <- whole$results |>
  select(id, area, length, width) |>
  left_join(whole$object_index, by = "id")
# HINT: yellow leaves have a negative NGRDI
leaf_traits |> filter(NGRDI < ___) |> select(id, NGRDI)      # TODO; you should get leaves 13 and 15
```

**Now your own eye.** Look at the labelled picture (`plot(fleaves)` above, or the right panel). Give each of the 15 leaves a **visual score of senescence**, 1 (green) to 5 (fully yellow), **without looking at the NGRDI**. Then compare with your neighbour.

```{r visual}
# TODO: type your 15 scores, in the order of the leaf ids 1 to 15
visual <- c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA)
leaf_traits$visual <- visual
cor(leaf_traits$visual, -leaf_traits$NGRDI, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
plot(leaf_traits$visual, leaf_traits$NGRDI, xlab = "Visual score", ylab = "NGRDI")
```

**Your findings:** does the image index agree with your eye? Where do you and your neighbour disagree with each other (the same leaf, a different score)? What does this say about the visual scores in your own trials? _...write here..._

# Disease severity

`measure_disease()` needs three small palettes: **healthy** tissue, **symptoms** and the **background**; the same palettes must be used for the whole study.

```{r severity, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 3.6}
set.seed(10)
leaf    <- image_pliman("sev_leaf_nb.jpg", plot = FALSE)
healthy <- image_pliman("sev_healthy.jpg", plot = FALSE)
lesions <- image_pliman("sev_sympt.jpg", plot = FALSE)
sev <- measure_disease(img = leaf, img_healthy = healthy, img_symptoms = lesions,
                       lesion_size = "large", plot = TRUE)
sev$severity     # about 10.7 % of the leaf area has symptoms
```

**Your findings:** would you trust this number for selection among M2 plants? What would you check first (palettes, lighting, a subset scored by an expert)? _...write here..._
